\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منافع} (munāfā)}{منافع (munāfā)}]{\ur{منافع} (munāfā) — a profit}

\label{lesson:UR-C419-munafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a payment, then the Urdu for to bring down (a price).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منافع}}
\textbf{\ur{منافع}} — \emph{munāfā} — \textquotedblleft{}a profit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{سال} \ur{دکان} \ur{کو} \ur{اچھا} \ur{منافع} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is sāl dukān ko achchhā munāfā huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shop made a good profit this year.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منافع}} (\emph{munāfā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{manāfiʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}benefits, gains\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munāfā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munāfā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is sāl dukān ko achchhā munāfā huā.} — The shop made a good profit this year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a payment, then the Urdu for to bring down (a price), then say \emph{munāfā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{منافع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A profit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خسارہ} (khasārā)}{خسارہ (khasārā)}]{\ur{خسارہ} (khasārā) — a business loss}

\label{lesson:UR-C419-khasara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to bring down (a price), then the Urdu for a profit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خسارہ}}
\textbf{\ur{خسارہ}} — \emph{khasārā} — \textquotedblleft{}a business loss\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بارش} \ur{کی} \ur{وجہ} \ur{سے} \ur{کسانوں} \ur{کو} \ur{خسارہ} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bārish kī vajah se kisānoṅ ko khasārā huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The farmers made a loss because of the rain.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خسارہ}} (\emph{khasārā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khasāra}, \textquotedblleft{}a loss\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سرمایہ} (sarmāyā)}{سرمایہ (sarmāyā)}]{\ur{سرمایہ} (sarmāyā) — capital (money); funds}

\label{lesson:UR-C419-sarmaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a profit, then the Urdu for a business loss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سرمایہ}}
\textbf{\ur{سرمایہ}} — \emph{sarmāyā} — \textquotedblleft{}capital (money); funds\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکان} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{سرمایہ} \ur{چاہیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukān ke liye sarmāyā chāhiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
You need capital to open a shop.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سرمایہ}} (\emph{sarmāyā}) is built from Persian \emph{sar}, \textquotedblleft{}a head\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{māya}, \textquotedblleft{}substance\textquotedblright{}: it is usually traced to Persian \emph{sarmāya}, \textquotedblleft{}capital\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اثاثہ} (asāsā)}{اثاثہ (asāsā)}]{\ur{اثاثہ} (asāsā) — an asset}

\label{lesson:UR-C419-asasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a business loss, then the Urdu for capital (money).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اثاثہ}}
\textbf{\ur{اثاثہ}} — \emph{asāsā} — \textquotedblleft{}an asset\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{مکان} \ur{ہمارا} \ur{سب} \ur{سے} \ur{بڑا} \ur{اثاثہ} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih makān hamārā sab se baṛā asāsā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This house is our biggest asset.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اثاثہ}} (\emph{asāsā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{athātha}, \textquotedblleft{}household goods\textquotedblright{}; Urdu says its \textbf{\ur{ث}} as an \emph{s}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سمیٹنا} (sameṭnā)}{سمیٹنا (sameṭnā)}]{\ur{سمیٹنا} (sameṭnā) — to pack up; to gather up}

\label{lesson:UR-C419-sametna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for capital (money), then the Urdu for an asset.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سمیٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سمیٹنا}} — \emph{sameṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pack up; to gather up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{شام} \ur{کو} \ur{دکاندار} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنا} \ur{سامان} \ur{سمیٹا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shām ko dukāndār ne apnā sāmān sameṭā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the evening the shopkeeper packed up his goods.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کپڑے} \ur{سمیٹے}, \emph{us ne kapṛe sameṭe}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سمیٹنا}} (\emph{sameṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{sameṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to roll up\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{saṃveṣṭayati}, \textquotedblleft{}wraps up\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13026).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sameṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shām ko dukāndār ne apnā sāmān sameṭā.} — In the evening the shopkeeper packed up his goods.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for capital (money), then the Urdu for an asset, then say \emph{sameṭnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
